key_insight: FL4N represents a changing 3D scene in a unified latent representation rather than explicit 4D primitives. The authors introduce it as the first feed-forward latent model for rendering dynamic scenes from new viewpoints and at different times.
problem_solved: 4D novel view synthesis must infer both 3D structure and motion from monocular input. Existing feed-forward approaches using explicit 4D Gaussians can produce temporal inconsistencies and severe rendering artifacts.
method: Use a feed-forward model for 4D novel view synthesis.
Encode a 4D scene prior into a unified latent representation instead of explicit 4D Gaussian primitives.
Target rendering across viewpoints and timestamps; further architecture details are not provided in the truncated abstract.
impact: FL4N offers practitioners an alternative representation for dynamic-scene synthesis that aims to address limitations of explicit Gaussian methods. The supplied abstract does not include results establishing quality or efficiency gains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular dynamic-scene input → unified 4D latent representation → novel-view renders at selected times.
Side-by-side concept illustration: explicit 4D Gaussian primitives versus a unified latent scene representation.
Viewpoint-by-time grid showing the two dimensions that 4D synthesis must handle.
Challenge icons highlighting 3D structure, temporal consistency, and rendering artifacts.
paper_title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Eunbeen Hong, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jooho Son, Hyunah Ko
